# zen-proxy

> A local, zero-dependency proxy that lets **any** coding agent use opencode's anonymous **free** Zen models — no accounts, no API keys. It speaks **two wire formats**: the OpenAI API (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/models`) for Cline, Roo Code, Continue, Aider, mimo CLI and opencode forks, and the **Anthropic Messages API** (`/v1/messages`) so **Claude Code works as-is**, tools included. For Claude Code it is a single command: `zen-claude`.

## The problem this solves

opencode's Zen gateway serves its free models (`big-pickle`, `space-bunny-free`, `nemotron-*-free`, `deepseek-*-free`, etc. — the exact set changes; `GET /v1/models` is authoritative) **only to requests that mimic the opencode client**.

- Since OpenCode 2, the gate reads far more than headers. A request that passes needs **all** of, measured against the live gateway with a byte-capture of OpenCode 2.1.4:
  - `POST https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1/chat/completions` with `Authorization: Bearer public` — the v2 base; `/inference/v1` answers `/models` only.
  - To run **under Bun**: the gate fingerprints the TLS/HTTP stack, and the identical request that streams `200` under Bun's fetch is bucketed **`429 FreeUsageLimitError`** from Node's.
  - The v2 wire identity: `x-opencode-client: cli`, `x-opencode-project` (sha1 hex), `b3`/`traceparent`, the session pair plus the `x-session-affinity`/`x-session-id` pair, UA `opencode/latest/<version>/cli`.
  - The **OpenCode harness system text** verbatim: a generic system prompt, the opening line, or a ~1.8 KB prefix of the harness text are all refused (`FreeUsageLimitError` with a `retry-after` window, indistinguishable from an exhausted quota) while the full text streams 200.
  - OpenCode's own tool manifest (the bare `read` stub the v1 gate accepted is not enough), `stream: true`, and a real `max_completion_tokens`.
  - Identity-level pacing: ~8 model probes fired concurrently from one session get blanket-`403 FreeTierError`'s; the same requests ~0.4 s apart pass.
- Missing session headers still return **400 MissingSessionID**; half a pair returns **403 FreeTierError**.
- The legacy `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1` and `/inference/v1` bases answer `/models` but the served agent base is `https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1`.
- Most agents force their own UA and system prompt, so they cannot use the free tier directly.

zen-proxy solves this by running under bun, injecting the CLI's full wire identity, prepending the captured harness preamble to every request, attaching OpenCode's v2 manifest and renaming the resulting calls back, then re-exposing everything on `http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1` — as either a standard OpenAI API or a standard Anthropic Messages API.

## Key facts

- **Endpoints**: `POST /v1/chat/completions` (stream + non-stream), `POST /v1/responses` (reads either dialect: a real Responses body gets Responses replies, a chat-shaped body keeps chat replies), `GET /v1/models`, `GET /health`, dashboard at `GET /`.
- **Auth**: anonymous via `Bearer public`; BYOK via `defaultZenKey` config or an `x-zen-key` / real bearer token. If a 429 says the identity's *own* free allowance is spent (the "Free usage limit reached" upgrade pitch, not the shared-bucket cooldown), that same attempt is retried once under the configured key before the chain moves on.
- **Session & identity**: the free tier tracks usage per session+project pair, not per key — upstream reads one pair as one CLI conversation in one project. The proxy mints the whole pair per caller (CLI-shaped session id + CLI-derived project hash, keyed by source IP + UA family: two different agents on one machine are two callers, a version bump is not a new one) and rotates both halves together every 30 minutes. A client that brings its own `x-opencode-session` / `x-opencode-project` is forwarded untouched; `injectSession: false` disables injection; `overrideSession: true` goes the other way and ignores the caller's pair, always speaking as the proxy's own rotating identity (handy for an OpenCode client you want raced per Tor lane). Nothing about IPs is rotated by the identity layer — `trustForwarded` stays in charge of how real IPs travel, and per-IP usage accounting is left exactly as it is. With `torEnabled` the exit really does change per lane (opt-in, see Tor exit lanes above).
- **Quota**: the free tier is per-IP (200 requests/day, resetting 00:00 UTC); the proxy forwards the real client IP (`x-real-ip`/`x-forwarded-for` when `trustForwarded` is on), but for local/loopback clients it omits `x-real-ip` so upstream counts your machine's real IP — matching opencode direct usage and avoiding a bogus shared `127.0.0.1` bucket. Do not abuse or rotate IPs.
- **Tor exit lanes (opt-in, off by default)**: `torEnabled` / `TOR=1` spreads the daily allowance over a fleet of local `tor` processes, one per exit relay. Each lane is its own tor process in its own data dir pinned to a distinct relay; a model call is raced down `torRaceWidth` (5) lanes at once and the first `200` keeps the client while the rest are cut. Five is measured, not shy — the gate refuses a client it sees arrive from half a dozen addresses for one session (`403 FreeTierError`), and refuses it through every exit afterwards. Refusals are charged per exit (429 sits the exit out until 00:00 UTC, burst 429 ~25 min, gate 403 5 min); lanes move to a fresh relay after `torExitSoftCap` requests (100) or `torExitHoldS` seconds (600), because the only way to learn an exit is spent is to be refused. Exits are drawn uniformly among the least-used relays across the whole country pool (so lanes spread across countries/ASes, not one country), and a live fleet keeps rotating refused exits and retrying until a lane wins — bounded by `torRetryMs` — never falling back to the device's own address while Tor is on. With `torSticky` (or `TOR_STICKY=1`) the race is replaced by a single exit ridden until the gate refuses it, then the next hot lane takes over — one tunnel spent at a time, so a working exit is never fanned out and the rest of the fleet stays unspent. Each lane mints its own session+project pair and rotates it with the exit; a caller-owned `x-opencode-session` is the exception — pinned to one lane, never fanned out, unless `overrideSession` is set. Bun's `fetch` tunnels via HTTP CONNECT to the lane's `HTTPTunnelPort`, so only the exit IP changes and the TLS fingerprint is untouched. **Requires Bun** (Node's `fetch` accepts a `proxy` option and silently ignores it, so lanes refuse to start under Node; BYOK still works there without lanes) and a `tor` binary — the first enabled run downloads the Tor Expert Bundle (~30 MB, once) into `torDataDir` (default: OS temp dir) unless a `tor` on `PATH` (0.4.8+) or an explicit `torBinary` is usable; an older tor is detected and skipped. Tor is slow and shared: this keeps work going when one address hits the wall, not a way to evade a ban. Ledger: `torDataDir/tor-ledger.json`.
- **Anthropic API**: `POST /v1/messages` (+ `/v1/messages/count_tokens`) are translated to the target model's endpoint family and back, streaming included, so Claude Code can point at it via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787` (the `zen-claude` command sets this for you). Because the free tier only accepts requests carrying opencode's own tools and its harness system text, the proxy attaches opencode's full manifest ahead of the caller's tools and prepends the harness preamble ahead of the caller's system prompt (everything the client sent still follows, nothing is dropped).
- **Model fallback**: reads the free-model list from `models.json`, which a GitHub Action keeps current from opencode's public catalog every 6 hours. Tries them in order on 429/5xx **and** on model-level 4xx (`Model is unavailable`, `FreeTierError`, geo-blocked or unsupported models), honors `retry-after`.
- **Claude Code, one command**: run `zen-claude`. There is no separate step — it starts the proxy if it is not already running, waits for it to answer, registers every live free Zen model in Claude Code's `/model` picker, launches Claude Code, and stops the proxy again when you exit. The installer puts `zen-claude` on your PATH (Linux/macOS and Windows alike, alongside `zen-proxy`; `claude-zen` is linked too as an alias). If Claude Code is not installed it says so, prints `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`, and exits without starting a proxy. It passes `claude --settings <file>` rather than exported env, because Claude Code reads env from `~/.claude/settings.json` and that wins over your shell; your existing Claude Code config is never modified.
- **Endpoint routing**: Zen serves each model on either `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/responses`. `responsesModels` lists the patterns (`*` allowed); the proxy translates requests, tool calls, reasoning and SSE streams in both directions, so any OpenAI-compatible client works either way.
- **Free-tier gate**: opencode serves free models only to traffic indistinguishable from its own client. Since OpenCode 2 that requires the v2 base, Bun's TLS/H2 fingerprint, the full harness preamble in the system text, OpenCode's own manifest (the bare `read` stub era is over), and CLI-grade identity headers; any of these missing lands in a shared `429 FreeUsageLimitError` (`retry-after` window, no personal usage involved) or `403 FreeTierError`. zen-proxy duplicates all of it (see the gate breakdown above). For replies: requests that bring no tools of their own — an agent's internal summarization/title call — keep `tool_choice: "none"` (the Responses API takes only "auto") and any manifest tool call in the reply is stripped, since such a caller cannot run one; providers also invent tool names sometimes (`client_nonce_lookup` streamed through once), so the per-request rule is: a reply keeps only the calls the caller actually offered. Requests that pin a tool of their own keep the pin; a pinned reply is filtered back down to the pinned call on every route (streaming included), and a reply whose every call got dropped ends as a plain stop. Normal agents keep their calls — manifest calls with a real counterpart are renamed back (`read`→`Read`, argument remaps included), and the rest never reach them.
- **Rate limiting**: optional per-client limit on chat requests (`rateLimitMax`, `0` = off). Local callers are split by user-agent family, so several agents behind one address do not share a budget. `/health` and the dashboard are never throttled; `/health` never calls upstream and reports the last known catalog state.
- **Model aliases**: `modelAliases` maps any name (e.g. `gpt-4o`) to a free model; reply model is rewritten back.
- **Config**: `zen-proxy.json` (hot-reloaded) or env vars: `PORT`, `HOST`, `ZEN_URL`, `ZEN_UA`, `INJECT_SESSION`, `OVERRIDE_SESSION` `AUTO_UA`, `UA_REFRESH_MS`, `PROBE_AUTH`, `RESPONSES_MODELS`, `RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, `DEFAULT_MODEL`, `FALLBACK_MODELS`, `MODEL_ALIASES`, `PROXY_KEY`, `ZEN_KEY`, `TRUST_FORWARDED`, `TIMEOUT_MS`, `CACHE_MS`, `AUTO_SYNC`, `AUTO_SYNC_MS`, `TOR`, `TOR_STICKY`, `TOR_LANES`, `TOR_RACE_WIDTH`, `TOR_COUNTRIES`, `TOR_FALLBACK_COUNTRIES`, `TOR_PREFERRED_COUNTRIES`, `TOR_SWEEP_S`, `TOR_SWEEP_MOVES`, `TOR_EXIT_SOFT_CAP`, `TOR_EXIT_HOLD_S`, `TOR_ROUNDS`, `TOR_STREAM_GRACE_S`, `TOR_MAX_CIRCUIT_DIRTINESS`, `TOR_BIN`, `TOR_DATA_DIR`, `TOR_DOWNLOAD`, `TOR_PROOF`, `TOR_STRICT_NODES`, `ZEN_PROXY_CONFIG`.
- **Auto model sync**: probes every upstream free model with the same agent-shaped request a real v2 client sends (harness preamble, OpenCode's manifest, `stream_options`, a real ask) — serially, with a beat between hops, because a rapid model-hop burst from one identity is blanket-403'd — and updates the config automatically. A `429 FreeUsageLimitError` is a shared-bucket condition, not model health: such probes land in `rate-limited`, never in the fail counter, so a model can no longer be silently removed after three syncs. Only definitively-gone models (`not supported`, 404) are removed from the user's list. `probeAuth` picks the probe credentials (`auto` / `anonymous` / `key`). A GitHub Action keeps the shipped catalog current too.
- **Requirements**: Bun >= 1.2 for the anonymous free tier (the gate 429s Node's TLS fingerprint); Node.js >= 18 still works with a real Zen key (BYOK). Zero npm dependencies.

## Install

```bash
# Linux / macOS
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/12errh/zen-proxy/main/install.sh | bash

# Windows (PowerShell)
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/12errh/zen-proxy/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

Or clone and run: `git clone https://github.com/12errh/zen-proxy.git && cd zen-proxy && bun zen-proxy.mjs`

## Point any agent at it

```jsonc
{
  "provider": {
    "zen": {
      "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1",
      "apiKey": "public",
      "models": { "space-bunny-free": {} }
    }
  }
}
```

Quick test:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"space-bunny-free","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}]}'
```
